title: ICSE CLASS 3 — Environmental Studies | Pollution Prevention
description: Subject-wise test on Pollution Prevention (Environmental Studies) for ICSE CLASS 3. 40Q.
subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: What is the main source of smoke that causes air pollution in cities?

options.explanation: Cooking at home is not a major contributor to air pollution in cities.
Factories and vehicles are major sources of air pollution in cities.
People breathing is not a major contributor to air pollution in cities.
Trees and plants are not sources of air pollution, they help clean the air.

questions.explanation: Factories release harmful gases and smoke, and vehicles burn fuel, releasing exhaust fumes that are major contributors to air pollution.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: Which of the following actions helps to prevent land pollution?

options.explanation: Throwing garbage on the road contributes to land pollution.

options.text: Burning dry leaves in the open
options.explanation: Burning dry leaves in the open can contribute to air pollution and does not prevent land pollution.

options.text: Putting all waste in a dustbin
options.explanation: Putting all waste in a dustbin helps prevent land pollution by keeping the surroundings clean.
Using plastic bags for everything can contribute to plastic pollution and does not prevent land pollution.

questions.explanation: Proper disposal of waste in dustbins prevents litter from accumulating on the ground and polluting the soil.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: Why should we turn off the tap while brushing our teeth?

options.explanation: The temperature of the water is not the reason to turn off the tap while brushing teeth.

options.text: To save water and prevent wastage
options.explanation: Turning off the tap while brushing teeth saves water and prevents unnecessary wastage.
The noise level in the bathroom is not the primary reason to turn off the tap while brushing teeth.
Cleaning the sink is not the reason to turn off the tap while brushing teeth.

questions.explanation: Turning off the tap prevents unnecessary water flow, which helps conserve this important natural resource and prevents water wastage.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: If you have an old plastic bottle, what is the best way to handle it to prevent pollution?

options.text: Throw it in the regular dustbin
options.explanation: Throwing a plastic bottle in the regular dustbin can contribute to plastic pollution in landfills.
Throwing a plastic bottle in a river contributes to water pollution and harms aquatic life.
Burning a plastic bottle releases harmful gases and contributes to air pollution.

options.text: Put it in a recycling bin
options.explanation: Recycling a plastic bottle helps prevent pollution by reusing the material.

questions.explanation: Recycling plastic bottles helps convert them into new products, reducing waste in landfills and preventing plastic pollution.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: Which of these contributes the most to noise pollution?

options.explanation: Birds chirping is a natural sound and is not considered noise pollution.
Loud music played from speakers is a common source of noise pollution.
Rain falling gently is a natural sound and is not considered noise pollution.
People talking softly is not typically considered noise pollution.

questions.explanation: Excessive and unwanted sound, such as loud music, is a primary cause of noise pollution, which can be harmful to living beings.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: Why is planting more trees important for preventing pollution?

options.explanation: Trees can provide shade and cool the air, but making the air warmer is not their primary role in preventing pollution.
Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, they do not release harmful gases.

options.text: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and clean the air
options.explanation: Trees are natural air purifiers, absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen, which helps reduce air pollution.
Trees do not typically make noise, and their presence can actually reduce noise pollution by acting as a natural barrier.

questions.explanation: Trees act as natural air purifiers, absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen, which helps reduce air pollution.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: Your mother is going to the market. What should she carry to avoid creating plastic waste?

options.explanation: Using many small plastic bags contributes to plastic pollution.
Using a new plastic container can contribute to plastic pollution if it is not reusable or recyclable.
Using a reusable cloth bag reduces the need for single-use plastic bags and helps prevent plastic pollution.
While an empty cardboard box can be reused, it may not be the most practical or convenient option for carrying items at the market.

questions.explanation: Using a reusable cloth bag reduces the need for single-use plastic bags, which are a major source of plastic pollution.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: A factory is releasing its waste directly into a nearby pond. What kind of pollution is this causing?

options.explanation: Releasing waste into a pond does not directly cause air pollution.
Releasing waste into a pond does not directly cause noise pollution.
Releasing waste into a pond contaminates the water, leading to water pollution.
While the waste may eventually affect the land surrounding the pond, the primary pollution caused by releasing waste into a pond is water pollution.

questions.explanation: When waste is released directly into a body of water like a pond, it contaminates the water, leading to water pollution.
questions.subject: icse3-evs

questions.question: Statement 1: We should always throw fruit peels and leftover food into a compost pit. Statement 2: Fruit peels and leftover food are biodegradable and can turn into useful manure for plants. Which of the following is true?

options.text: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true.
options.explanation: Statement 1 is true, as throwing biodegradable waste into a compost pit is a good practice.

options.text: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false.
options.explanation: Statement 2 is true, as fruit peels and leftover food are biodegradable and can turn into useful manure for plants.
Both statements are true, as throwing biodegradable waste into a compost pit is a good practice and fruit peels and leftover food are biodegradable.

options.text: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 explains Statement 1.
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 explains why Statement 1 is a good practice.

questions.explanation: Throwing biodegradable waste like fruit peels and leftover food into a compost pit is a good practice. This is because they decompose naturally to form compost, which is a nutrient-rich manure for plants.

questions.question: Imagine you live near a construction site where machines are constantly making loud noises. What is the most likely negative effect of this on people living nearby?

options.explanation: Loud noise is unlikely to make people feel more energetic.

options.text: They might have trouble sleeping and concentrating.
options.explanation: Loud noise can disrupt sleep patterns and make it difficult for people to concentrate.

options.text: They will learn to like the loud noises.
options.explanation: People are unlikely to learn to like loud noises, especially if they are constant and disturbing.
Loud noise from construction does not directly improve air quality.

questions.explanation: Constant loud noise can be very disturbing and harmful, leading to problems like difficulty sleeping, stress, and trouble concentrating, especially in children.

questions.question: What makes the air dirty and difficult to breathe?

options.explanation: Fresh air from plants does not pollute the air.
Smoke released from vehicles, factories, and burning things contains harmful gases and particles that pollute the air.
Rainwater does not pollute the air.
Sunlight does not pollute the air.

questions.explanation: Smoke released from vehicles, factories, and burning things contains harmful gases and particles that pollute the air, making it unhealthy to breathe.

questions.question: Where should we throw garbage to prevent land pollution and keep our surroundings clean?

options.explanation: Throwing garbage on the road contributes to land pollution.
Throwing garbage in a river contributes to water pollution.
Throwing garbage in a dustbin prevents land pollution.
Throwing garbage out of the window contributes to land pollution.

questions.explanation: Throwing garbage in a dustbin ensures it is collected and disposed of properly, preventing it from littering the land and causing pollution.

questions.question: If you see someone throwing plastic bottles and wrappers into a lake, what kind of pollution are they causing?

options.explanation: Air pollution is not caused by throwing waste into a lake.
Noise pollution is not caused by throwing waste into a lake.

questions.question: Which of these is a good way to save water and prevent wastage at home?

options.text: Leaving the tap running while brushing teeth
options.explanation: Leaving the tap running wastes water.

questions.question: Assertion: We should plant more trees in our neighbourhood. Reason: Trees help to clean the air by absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen. Which of the following is true?

questions.question: What is the main cause of noise pollution in busy cities?

options.explanation: Quiet libraries and parks do not contribute to noise pollution.
Birds chirping in gardens do not contribute to noise pollution.

options.text: Loud horns from vehicles and construction sounds
options.explanation: Loud horns and construction sounds are major sources of noise pollution.

questions.question: Your school is planning an activity to celebrate 'Earth Day'. Which activity would best help in preventing pollution?

options.text: Playing very loud music in the school ground

options.text: Burning dry leaves in a pile

options.text: Planting saplings (young trees) in the school garden

questions.question: Which of these actions does NOT help in preventing pollution?

options.text: Using cloth bags instead of plastic bags for shopping
options.explanation: Using cloth bags helps in reducing plastic waste and preventing pollution.

options.text: Turning off lights and fans when leaving a room
options.explanation: Turning off lights and fans helps in conserving energy and reducing pollution.

options.text: Throwing fruit peels and vegetable scraps on the street
options.explanation: Throwing fruit peels and vegetable scraps on the street contributes to land pollution.

options.text: Recycling old newspapers and plastic bottles

questions.question: Riya lives near a busy road and a factory. She often hears loud noises and sees thick smoke coming from the factory chimney. Her younger brother sometimes coughs a lot. What is the most likely environmental problem in Riya's neighbourhood?

options.explanation: Too much sunlight is not indicated by the description.
The presence of thick smoke indicates air pollution, not clean air.
The description indicates both air and noise pollution.

questions.question: The '3 R's' (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle) are important for pollution prevention. Why is 'Reduce' considered the most important 'R' to start with?

options.text: Because it encourages making new things from old materials.
options.explanation: This describes 'Reuse', not 'Reduce'.

options.text: Because it means buying fewer new things and creating less waste in the first place.
options.explanation: 'Reduce' is about minimizing waste generation.

options.text: Because it focuses on using items again and again.
options.explanation: This describes 'Reuse', not 'Reduce'.

options.text: Because it is the easiest way to clean up existing pollution.
options.explanation: 'Reduce' is about preventing pollution, not cleaning up existing pollution.

questions.explanation: 'Reduce' is the most important because it addresses the root cause of pollution by minimizing the generation of waste from the very beginning.

options.explanation: Resources are not harmful substances.

questions.question: To prevent pollution effectively and keep our community clean in the most comprehensive way, which habit is most crucial for every citizen to adopt?

options.text: Using only public transport instead of personal cars.

options.text: Turning off lights and fans when not in use.

options.text: Segregating waste at home into different bins for recycling and composting.
options.explanation: While all options contribute to pollution prevention, segregating waste at home (C) is the most comprehensive as it directly addresses land pollution, reduces the burden on landfills, facilitates recycling (saving resources and reducing industrial pollution), and enables composting (benefiting soil). This single habit has a wide-ranging positive impact on multiple types of pollution.

options.text: Avoiding loud music and noise from crackers.
